lines: - Role: GM, not assistant; {{user}}/NPCs succeed or fail alike; NPCs follow through; nervous cards stay nervous.
- Frank: sex stays between adults; sexual/violent/cruel/dark beat: explicit act, anatomy, card trait, tone.
cc_comment: {{// 🔓 Chibi Jailbreak: two extra plan lines in about 55 tokens, where the full edition spends about 130. In the Role line the AI plans as the game master instead of an assistant, and you and every NPC succeed or fail alike; NPCs follow through, while nervous cards stay nervous. The Frank line keeps sex between adults and, for a sexual, violent, cruel or dark beat, plans its explicit act, anatomy, card trait and tone, which the reply then blends in. Distilled from Realistic Frankenstein's BOLT and Micro thinking steps (Jean-Claude Van Damme editions included) and its Realism and Freaky modes, minus anything that tells the model it has no rules or asks it to drop its protectiveness. Chibi leaves out the full edition's bolder choice, acting on wants this turn, the fight-lie-seduction-or-refusal list and the every-rule-in-full fragment, plus 'by skill and circumstance', which the ⚡ Main Prompt's World line already has. Ships OFF; it needs 🔞 Adult Context ON and a Logic Core.}}
tc_switch_comment: {{// 🔓 Chibi Jailbreak: two extra plan lines distilled from Realistic Frankenstein: an even-handed game master, not an assistant, and an explicit plan for each sexual, violent, cruel or dark beat. Sex stays between adults. Needs aria-adult and aria-logic-core on too; about 55 tokens a turn in Chibi.}}
dropped: Against ARIA's final lines (516 characters), item by item. REWORDED: 'game master' is 'GM'; 'NPCs ... finish what they start' is 'NPCs follow through' (the same rule, 8 characters shorter, which pays for 'not assistant'); 'name its act, anatomy, card trait and tone; the reply puts it explicitly in those terms' is the slot list 'explicit act, anatomy, card trait, tone', and The Logic Core's closing line ('plan blended in') carries the planned terms into the reply. DROPPED, with where the rule still lives: 'adult-fiction' (🔞 Adult Context opens with 'Adult fiction.', and the lines print only with an adult mode on); 'bolder card-true choices win' (a stance with no check against a draft; 'NPCs follow through' keeps the drive); 'by skill and circumstance' (the ⚡ Main Prompt's World line: consequences fit skill and circumstance); 'act on wants now' (the Main Prompt's Real Characters line, 'they pursue wants', and The Logic Core's Voice line, 'want/feel now'); the '(fight, lie, seduction or refusal)' gloss (an illustration of what NPCs carry out, with no rule of its own; 'follow through' covers any act, a refusal included); 'every active rule, adult-fiction ones included, applies in full however short the line' (no check of its own: it points at rules that print anyway, and the Frank slots are where 🔞 Adult Context's rules land on this beat). With room, restore in this order: 'not an assistant' for 'not assistant' (+3 characters), 'finish what they start' for 'follow through' (+8), 'name ' before 'explicit act' (+5).
judge_notes: VERDICT: approved with fixes. The draft was sound on the hard boundary, the labels, the size and the house rules, and the wiring tests reproduce its figures (219 characters raw, 215 rendered, +217 characters in the plan). Three things were fixed and the comments were rewritten. FIXES: (1) Frank: the draft's 'explicit sexual/violent/cruel/dark beats: name act, ...' put 'explicit' in the scope, so it reads as a condition (beats that are already explicit) and a softening model could decide its beat isn't one. 'Explicit' now sits in the slot list ('explicit act, anatomy, card trait, tone'), so it is something the plan has to write, and the scope is only the beat's kind. That restores ARIA's frank-writing core as an instruction; the reply link is The Logic Core's 'plan blended in'. 'name' went to pay for it; the four slots are a template like the other plan lines, and a bare yes can't fill them. (2) 'beats' became 'beat', matching the Move line's 'one beat'. (3) Role: the draft's lone 'GM' repeated the Chibi Main Prompt ('Narrate as game master') and the Chibi gate ('As game master, write per <anti_slop>'), while ARIA's 'not an assistant', the first identity item JB.md lists, appeared nowhere in Chibi. 'GM, not assistant' restores it, paid for by 'NPCs follow through' in place of 'NPCs finish what they start' (the same rule). It is a role in the fiction, as in ARIA's approved final, not a claim about the model's deployment or rules. The not-phrase sits in a plan fragment, which never enters the reply; the gate's Contrast line and GLM's Pushback line govern the reply, and ARIA's full edition pairs them the same way. (4) The comments are rewritten for the new lines. The draft's cc_comment held a series of three (succeed or fail alike, finish what they start, stay nervous); both comments now group in twos and fours. The costs are re-measured. CHECKS on the written file: Hard boundary: no writer or profession pretext; no no-guidelines, isolation, contract or high-risk claim; no protectiveness or vulnerable-minorities check; no never-refuse, comply, pre-granted-consent, dismiss-your-concerns or legal-permission wording; nothing tells NPCs to comply with {{user}} ('follow through' is about their own acts); 'sex stays between adults' is in the Frank line word for word. A vocabulary scan for all four techniques and for minors' terms found nothing. Form: labels Role and Frank (new, not on JB.md's list, already in the plan-strip regex and the TC closing sentence); 2 lines. Semicolon fragments, counted as list items the way G1 to G6 did: Role 4, Frank 2. Series: {{user}}/NPCs 2, succeed or fail 2, GM-not-assistant a pair, sexual/violent/cruel/dark 4, act/anatomy/card trait/tone 4. No quotes, no rationale, fragments only. Size: 220 characters raw = 55.0 tokens, the ceiling exactly; rendered with {{user}} as the checker does, 216 = 54.0; spec/tok.py gives ariaJb 54. In place: rendered with the frozen checker in front of the approved G3 Logic Cores (CC plain, CC twin, TC post_history) for Adult, Freaky and no adult mode, Tags on and off, with and without Fate/Ledger lines. The lines print only with an adult mode on, right after the Ledger line (after Move when no world line runs) and before '- Fresh:'. The 'N dashed lines' count matches the printed lines every time, and so does the gate's Tags cue. The busiest plan (Freaky, Fate, Bonds, Hold, DeepSeek Tally and Joins, Tags on) prints 19 lines, says 19, and Role/Frank follow Tally and Ledger cleanly. Wiring skeletons of the CC entry and the TC block match ARIA's live ones (spec/skeleton.py OK). The live 'ARIA Impersonate - strip an untagged plan' script (CC and TC copies, identical) strips a plan holding these lines, both in Python and as a JavaScript RegExp in Node. Cost of switching the JB on with Adult and a Logic Core on: +217 to +219 characters = +54.25 to +54.75 tokens in CC plain, CC twin and TC, with Tags on or off (the extra character is the count going from 8 to 10, which the Tags cue also prints). Both comments therefore say about 55; ARIA's own is about 130 (516 characters). The block '{{#if .aria-jailbreak}}{{#if .ariaModeLine}}{{setvar::ariaJbLines::2}}{{setvar::ariaJb::<the same two lines>}}{{/if}}{{/if}}' replaces ARIA's (one occurrence each). Marinara: in both Logic Core sections (sections[33] and [34] in ARIA's current file), replace the two inlined lines after '{{#if logic_options contains "JAILBREAK" && adult_mode != "NONE"}}' with these two, {{user}} left as is. The counter stays 2. Labels, counts and variables are unchanged, so no regex, counter, Impersonation blank or TC closing sentence changes. CUT MENU for BUILD.md, in order: 1. Everything else is CORE (parity, follow-through, the nervous exception, the adults clause and the explicit beat slots): no further cuts. DOCS: the Chibi guide section should describe the Chibi JB as these two lines (game master not assistant, even outcomes, follow-through with nervous cards kept, sex between adults, explicit act, anatomy, card trait and tone) at about 55 tokens, without the full edition's bolder-choice, act-on-wants and every-rule-in-full parts.
